title: Apartment Painting Contractor in Gainesville & Ocala

sections.h2: Unit turns that keep the leasing calendar on track
body: In apartments, an empty unit is lost rent. When a resident moves out, painting is usually the step that decides how fast the unit is ready to show. As an apartment painting contractor in Gainesville, Ocala, and the surrounding area, we build turn work around your make-ready schedule, coordinating with cleaning, carpet, and maintenance so the paint crew is in and out in the right order.

Gainesville's student housing has a sharp turnover each summer, when many units empty at once and have to be ready for the next lease start. We plan those peaks ahead with property managers so crews are staffed for them and units are not left waiting in line for paint.
bullets: Patch nail holes, anchor holes, and dings from move-out
Walls, ceilings, trim, and doors painted to the community standard
Kitchen and bath walls in a washable finish
Unit left clean and ready for the next make-ready step

body: Turn work rewards standardization. We keep your community's wall, ceiling, and trim formulas on file, along with the product and sheen for each, so any unit can be painted to spec and a touch-up eighteen months later still matches. When a unit only needs touch-ups between residents, the standard color means it can be spot-painted without repainting full walls.

If your properties are moving to a new standard palette, a color consultation can help pick durable, broadly appealing colors that hide wear and photograph well for listings. Pricing can be set up per unit or per building so turn budgets are predictable through the year.

Shared spaces are what prospective residents see on a tour. Breezeways, stairwells, corridors, mail areas, clubhouses, and fitness rooms take heavy traffic and need scrubbable finishes. Exterior breezeways and stair stringers also deal with weather, so they get coatings suited to outdoor exposure, and metal railings get direct-to-metal finishes rather than wall paint.

Common-area work is done in sections so residents can always get to their doors. Wet paint is marked, and stairwells stay passable at all times. Clubhouses and leasing offices are scheduled with the office staff so tours and resident events are not interrupted, often early in the week when traffic is lightest.

sections.h2: Interior wear and the problems we see most
body: Every community has its own pattern of wear, but a few problems come up in almost every unit. Walls next to entry doors and along hallways get scuffed by furniture during moves. Bathrooms show peeling paint near the shower where steam has no place to go, and our article on humidity and peeling paint explains why. Kitchen walls near the range collect grease that has to be cleaned before any new paint will hold. Ceilings in older buildings may show water stains from upstairs units or roof leaks, which need a stain-blocking primer.

We flag recurring issues to management. If the same bathroom wall peels in every unit of a building, the fix is likely a ventilation or product problem, not repeated repainting, and it is worth knowing before the next round of turns.

Repainting an occupied community is as much about communication as paint. We supply door notices ahead of each building, stage the work building by building, and coordinate with management on parking, pets, and patio items that need to be moved. Ladders, lifts, and open coatings are never left unattended in shared spaces overnight.

The exterior system follows the building: elastomeric on stucco and block with hairline cracking, 100% acrylic on siding and trim, and metal finishes on railings. Buildings are washed first; see our pressure washing service. Our commercial exterior painting page covers access and phasing on larger buildings. Exterior work carries a written workmanship warranty of up to 10 years.

Property managers and owners need clean paperwork. We provide a certificate of insurance naming your entity before mobilization, and every crew member is covered by workers' compensation. Proposals are itemized by building, area, or unit type, with products and coats spelled out. For associations and managed portfolios beyond apartments, see HOA and property management painting, and our guide to hiring licensed painters for an HOA covers what boards should ask for.
Drywall damage beyond normal turn patching can be handled through our drywall repair service. Local information is on our Gainesville commercial painting page.

faqs.q: How fast can you turn an apartment unit?
faqs.a: It depends on unit size and condition, but we schedule turns around your make-ready calendar and coordinate with cleaning and flooring so the unit is ready to show as quickly as possible.

faqs.q: How do you keep paint colors consistent across units?
faqs.a: We keep your community's wall, ceiling, and trim formulas on file with product and sheen, so every unit and every touch-up matches the standard.

faqs.q: Can you paint apartment exteriors while residents live there?
faqs.a: Yes. We post door notices, work building by building, keep breezeways and stairwells passable, and never leave equipment unattended in shared spaces overnight.

faqs.q: Do you offer per-unit pricing for turns?
faqs.a: Yes. Turn pricing can be set up per unit or per building so your budget is predictable. We do not publish prices; the proposal is based on your unit types and standards.
